## The problem

Loom rotates Codex accounts by pointing `CODEX_HOME` at a per-account profile
directory under `~/.loom/codex-profiles/`. The Codex CLI reads **everything**
from that directory — `AGENTS.md`, `config.toml` (models, MCP servers, sandbox
defaults), `prompts/`, `hooks.json` — so a profile created by `accounts add`
and nothing else is a **blank install**. That is the concrete reason a pooled
non-default account behaves differently from the operator's own: no repo
instructions, no MCP servers, no managed `pre_tool_use` guard bridge.

Issue #8672 closes that gap.

## The sharing table

Provisioning is driven by a per-provider table
(`loom-daemon/src/tokens_pool/profile_sharing.rs`), not by Codex-specific code.
Each surface of the profile gets exactly one mechanism, chosen for a reason:

| Surface | Mechanism | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Capability dirs (`prompts/`, `skills/`, `plugins/`) | **symlink** to the default profile's dir | a live share: anything installed into the default later needs no re-sync |
| Session/history trees (`sessions/`, `archived_sessions/`) | **symlink** | append-only, so one `--resume` history across pooled accounts is safe, and is the point |
| Plain files (`AGENTS.md`, `instructions.md`) | **copy** | the CLIs write tmp-then-rename, which would *replace* a symlink with a regular file and silently fork the operator's original into a private copy |
| Settings (`config.toml`) | **key-merge** under a denylist | share configuration key by key; a wholesale copy would drag identity and trust state along with it |
| `hooks.json` | installed by `provision-codex-hooks.sh` | the managed `pre_tool_use` bridge already owns this file and preserves every operator entry; a second writer with its own idempotency record would fight it |
| `auth.json`, identity keys, per-project trust state | **never shared** | |

The TOML merge goes through a format-preserving document model
(`toml_edit`), so every key Loom does not own — comments, ordering and
whitespace included — survives byte-for-byte.

The **key denylist** is total, not top-level: recursion never stops early, so
`hooks.state."<id>".trusted_hash` is refused while the rest of `hooks` stays
shareable. A composite value (inline table, array of tables) that *contains* a
denied key is refused whole rather than spliced.

For Codex the denylist is `hooks.state`, `projects`, `account_id`,
`chatgpt_account_id`, `preferred_auth_method`, `api_key`, `openai_api_key`,
`credentials`, `auth`, `tokens`.

## The ledger: a local edit wins forever

`<profile>/.loom-profile.json` records the SHA-256 of each copied file, the
canonical value of each merged key, and each symlink's target. On the next run
Loom overwrites a surface **only while the profile still holds exactly what
Loom last wrote there.** The moment you edit a provisioned file or key by hand,
the fingerprint stops matching and that surface is yours permanently — no
future provisioning pass, including the one at daemon start, will touch it
again.

A surface that existed *before* Loom ever provisioned the profile has no ledger
entry either, so it is treated the same way: yours, untouched.

The ledger carries no timestamp and is rewritten only when its content actually
changes, which is what makes "the second run is a no-op" observable by mtime.

## When it runs

| Trigger | Scope |
|---|---|
| `accounts add` / `accounts import` | the profile just created, automatically |
| `accounts reauth` | the profile just logged back into, automatically |
| `accounts provision [--all\|<name>]` | on demand |
| daemon start (reconciliation pass) | every registered pooled profile |

The daemon-start pass is on by default because a profile created before this
shipped, or one that has drifted since the operator changed their own
`config.toml`, should not need anyone to remember a command. It is safe to run
unconditionally: it writes nothing when there is nothing to do, never
overwrites a local edit, never reads a credential, and skips session-managed
profiles (whose container owns the directory — issue #6925). Switch it off with
`LOOM_PROFILE_PROVISION_ON_START=0`.

## Using it

```bash
loom-daemon accounts provision --all                 # every registered account
loom-daemon accounts provision agent-1               # one account
loom-daemon accounts provision --all --dry-run       # report, write nothing
loom-daemon accounts provision --all --json          # machine-readable reports
loom-daemon accounts provision agent-1 --from ~/.codex-work   # explicit source
loom-daemon accounts provision --all --skip-hooks    # surfaces only
```

Exit codes: `0` every selected profile is provisioned or already up to date;
`1` at least one profile failed (each named on stderr, the rest still done);
anything else is the ordinary CLI error path.

**The default profile is never inferred from the ambient `CODEX_HOME`.** A
dispatched agent already has that pointed at a *pooled* profile, so trusting it
would make one pooled account the provisioning source for another. Resolution
is `--from`, else `LOOM_CODEX_DEFAULT_HOME`, else `~/.codex`. A source that
contains the target profile (or vice versa) is refused outright.

## What it will never do

- **Read or write a credential.** `auth.json` is on the provider's
  `never_share` list, is absent from its sharing table (asserted at startup by
  the table's own validator), and every path is re-checked immediately before
  it is opened.
- **Share hook trust.** Codex persists hook trust as
  `hooks.state."<id>".trusted_hash` in `config.toml`. Importing another
  profile's hashes would fake a trust decision that never happened for this
  profile, so those keys are denied. Trust stays a per-profile,
  operator-attested one-time step, and **Loom never passes
  `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`** — see
  [`guardrail-parity-codex.md`](guardrail-parity-codex.md).
- **Share per-project trust state.** `[projects."<path>"] trust_level` is
  denied for the same reason.
- **Touch a session-managed profile.** Once `accounts session start` adopts
  one, its container is the sole writer of that `CODEX_HOME`.
- **Delete anything.** Provisioning only adds and updates; a key the default
  profile dropped stays in the pooled profile.

## Adding another provider

Kimi (`KIMI_CODE_HOME`, issue #8628) and any future provider join as **data**:
a new `const ProviderProfileRules` in `profile_sharing.rs` plus a row in
`PROVIDER_RULES`. Nothing in the provisioner itself is provider-aware — its
test suite drives a synthetic non-Codex provider (different home variable,
different surfaces, a JSON settings document instead of TOML, its own denylist)
through the identical entry point to keep that true.

The one Codex-shaped detail is the **account registry**: `--all` can only
enumerate providers Loom tracks accounts for. A provider without one is still
provisionable, by path.
